evidence.ref: The WARP-0603 TrackerAdapter seam (.warp/tracker_adapter.py) gains assign(obj_id, assignee), a fifth explicit audited write beside comment/set_status/create_or_update_epic/create_or_update_child, with the SAME base-owned guarantees: it validates input BY NAME (a blank obj_id or assignee is a TrackerAdapterError via _require, before any surface call), FAILS LOUD on an object the tracker does not hold (TrackerItemNotFound, never a silent no-op), records the write in the base-owned writes() audit (_record 'assign'), and is idempotent by TARGET assignee (the subclass primitive _assign returns True on a real change, False when the object already holds that assignee). FakeTracker implements _assign in-memory (each record carries an 'assignee', added to _new_record; reassignment is idempotent by target) and the module docstring documents the guarantee. The live JiraCloudAdapter._assign and ConfluenceCloudAdapter._assign (.warp/tracker_intake.py) RAISE by name ('assignment against live Jira is wired in a later increment (WARP-1005)'; 'a wiki page has no assignee'), so the live path is NOT exercised here and the gate drives only the FakeTracker.

selftest (scripts/selftest.py, the WARP-1004 block) drives the FakeTracker through the op with teeth: a first assign to a differing assignee returns True, a repeat returns False (idempotent by target), the write appears in writes() as op 'assign' (explicit + audited), a blank assignee raises TrackerAdapterError by name, and an assign to a missing object raises TrackerItemNotFound by name. The adapter selfcheck also exercises assign (real change True, idempotent False).

The spec mirror (.warp/tracker_mirror.py) projects ARTIFACT LINKS onto the ticket at the build-complete / ready-to-test point (a spec entering review after a build, verdict.recorded -> in_review). It posts a KEYED comment (key '<sid>:artifacts', so at most once under at-least-once replay) whose text carries only the links that EXIST: the commit always, and the pull request and the proof WHEN present. _artifact_links(evs) gathers commit/pr/proof from the lifecycle events (latest non-empty wins) and NEVER fabricates a missing one - a commit-only build yields a comment with the commit and no invented PR or proof. It writes only a comment through the audited seam (never a spec or plan definition), so the repository stays the source of truth.

selftest asserts: at ready-to-test the artifact-links comment is posted exactly once (artifact_comments == 1) and its text carries the commit, the PR, and the proof when all three are on the event; a commit-only verdict yields a comment containing the commit and NEITHER 'pull request' NOR 'proof' text (no fabrication); a pre-ready-to-test point posts no links (artifact_comments == 0); and a replay posts no duplicate comment (idempotent by comment key, tracker state byte-identical).

At the ready-to-test handoff (verdict.recorded -> in_review, the one transition) the mirror REASSIGNS the child away from the single Agent user (WARP-1001 config 'agent') to the configured reviewer via the new assign seam op. resolve_reviewer(config, repo_id, reporter) resolves a per-repo 'reviewer' in .warp/trackers.json OVER a global 'reviewer', either falling back to the ticket's reporter (carried on the spec metadata, read by build_spec_index), and returns None (leaving the assignee UNTOUCHED, never inventing one) when none is known. The reassign is guarded (reviewer and reviewer != agent) so it never assigns TO the Agent, and is idempotent by target assignee. It hangs off ONLY the ready-to-test transition: an earlier lifecycle point (spec.ready) never reaches the reassign, so the fleet keeps the ticket while it works. The per-repo reviewer setting is documented and templated in plugin/templates/.warp/trackers.json (global 'reviewer' + per-repo override + _reviewer_comment).

selftest teeth: at ready-to-test the child is reassigned to the reviewer (defaulting to the ticket's reporter) exactly once (assignee == reporter, reassignments == 1); a pre-ready-to-test replay of spec.ready does NOT reassign and the Agent keeps it (assignee == agent, reassignments == 0); a NON-TAUTOLOGICAL pair proves causation (the same setup with the ready-to-test event removed keeps the Agent, adding it hands to the reviewer); a per-repo 'reviewer' overrides the reporter default (assignee == qa-lead); and a replay performs no duplicate reassignment (idempotent by target).

The gate-test over the FakeTracker has TEETH (scripts/selftest.py, WARP-1004 block, offline, no network): at the ready-to-test transition the ticket is reassigned to the reviewer (defaulting to the reporter) exactly once AND the artifact links are posted once; a lifecycle point BEFORE ready-to-test does NOT reassign and posts no links, proven NON-TAUTOLOGICALLY (removing the verdict.recorded event keeps the Agent, adding it hands to the reviewer); a re-run posts no duplicate comment and performs no duplicate reassignment (idempotent by comment key and by target assignee, tracker state byte-identical on replay); and an assign to a missing object fails loud (TrackerItemNotFound). The mirror selfcheck also covers the reporter-default handoff and its idempotency.
